newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to hold talks over Colombo port strike.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to hold talks over Colombo port strike.

text.p: Sri Lankan Ports and Shipping Minister Mohamed Ashraff is to hold talks with labour unions later on Thursday to try to avert a strike at Colombo port on Friday, a ministry spokesman said.

Two labour unions have said its members among the port's 16,000-strong work force will strike on Friday in protest against government plans to lease the Queen Elizabeth Quay to a consortium led by the Peninsula & Oriental Shipping Co.
The Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), which runs Colombo, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, is holding talks with P&O to set up a new container terminal to expand capacity.

The project, estimated to cost up to a billion dollars and take 10 years to build, will see the development of the southern part of the port. At least another six deep-draft berths are planned for fifth and sixth generation ships, with a capacity of two million containers a year.
The port, with a capacity of 1.6 million containers, handled 1.2 million containers up to the end of November. It handled 129,000 units handled in November alone, its highest monthly throughout.
The government has said it will go ahead with the P&O deal because of the urgent need to expand capacity to meet growing trans-shipment volumes.
The port recently cracked down on labour and announced new tariffs to improve services and attract bigger and more modern vessels.
